title: Hudson Canyon: down the wall

briefing.summary: Descend into Hudson Canyon and scan its steep north wall and a deeper coral-habitat ledge. The two scans reveal how the canyon slopes create different seafloor habitats.
facts: Hudson Canyon begins about 100 miles southeast of New York City and runs roughly 350 miles seaward; its lower reaches (beyond this survey tile) reach 2-2.5 miles (3,200-4,000 m) deep.
It is the drowned seaward extension of the ancestral Hudson River, carved into today's shape in part by a catastrophic glacial meltwater flood (USGS).
A NOAA-led sanctuary designation for Hudson Canyon is proposed, not yet finalized -- the process opened in 2022 and remains under review as of this survey.
Part of the canyon is already protected today: the Frank R. Lautenberg Deep Sea Coral Protection Area bans bottom-tending fishing gear across much of it.
hazards: Strong local currents along the canyon walls, especially near the shelf break.
Steep, rocky flanks (measured here at roughly 18-19 deg): watch altitude near the wall and coral-ledge scan points.
Active commercial fishing grounds -- expect gear and vessel traffic near the shelf in a real-world dive.

objectives.title: Scan the north canyon wall
objectives.hint: Find the steep north wall of the upper canyon, near 540 m.

objectives.title: Survey the coral ledge
objectives.hint: Follow the wall southeast to the coral-habitat ledge, around 940 m.

notable_species: deep-sea corals and sponges (Frank R. Lautenberg Deep Sea Coral Protection Area)
